Application for new party name for parliamentary elections

1. Information about the party 
 Party name:

The Synthetic Party

The party name must be stated precisely as the Election Committee will decide on it, and which, after possible approval, will appear on 
 the voter declaration portal. You cannot get a party name approved that is identical or confusable with the name of another party, 
 or which has special features, e.g. consisting only of capital letters. Read more on the next page under 3. Which party names 
 can be approved?

Party contact information:

You can provide an e-mail address, a postal address, or both. You can also add a phone number, but that alone is 
 not sufficient. The party's contact details will be published on the voter declaration portal if the party name is approved.

Link to the party's own page (optional):

computerlars.com

On voter declaration portals, the party can be listed with a link to the party's own page. This can, for example, be a link to the party's home
page or a page on social media where voters can read more about the party. Only one page can be specified.

Guidance for the application for approval of a new party name

1. New parties for parliamentary elections
For a new party to become eligible to stand for Folketing elections,
the party name must be approved by the Election Board.

When the Election Board has approved a new party name, the Ministry of the Interior and Housing creates
a collection for the party in the
voter declaration portal. Thereafter, voters can freely go
in and submit voter declarations for the party in the 3years during which
the Election Board's approval applies. Currently, a party must
collect 20.182voter declarations to be able to stand
for parliamentary election. The number is calculated after each parliamentary
election.

You can read more about how to form a new
party on the Ministry of the Interior and Housing's website
here.

2. Application for a new party name

Anyone who has the right to vote can apply to have a
new party name approved by filling out this application form and
sending it to the Election Board.

It is mandatory to use this form, and it is
important that you fill out all fields that are not marked as
optional. Otherwise, the Election Board cannot process your application.

You can send the application to:

Election Board, Ministry of the Interior and Housing
Holmens Kanal 22
1060 Copenhagen K

You can also send the application digitally. If you send
your application digitally, we recommend that you send it securely
via Digital Post, for example from your e-Boks. This way the
application is sent encrypted, and it is automatically
signed with your digital signature.

Both the applicant and the representative must sign
the application, if a representative for
the party is indicated. This can be done by hand or digitally. The application
can be signed digitally by both the appli[████] cant and the re
presentative, by both parties submitting each their
copy of the application via Digital Post.

Read more about how to send securely with Digital
Post on the Ministry of the Interior and Housing's website
here. If you have questions about the application[████], you can
call the Ministry of the Interior and Housing at tel. [████]
and ask to be connected to the Election Unit.

Applications for approval of a party name are processed
by the Electoral Committee about 6 times a year. When the Electoral Committee
has processed your application, you will be sent the decision
. You will receive it in your digital mailbox (e-
Boks), if you are registered for Digital Post. If you are exempt
from Digital Post, you will receive the decision by
mail.

3. Which party names can be approved?

It is important that voters do not confuse the parties on the ballot paper when there is an election. Therefore, the Election Board must approve the names of new parties, so they can begin to collect voter declarations.




On the Ministry of the Interior and Housing's website here you can
see a list of which party names are already
in use (the party name register), and which you therefore cannot get
approved. You also cannot get approval for a party name
that can be confused with one of these. Before you submit an
application to the Election Board, it is a good idea to check
[████]whether the party name or a similar party name is already
approved.

The Election Board also does not approve party names that contain offensive words, conflict with acceptable language use, or are highlighted with special features, e.g., by being written exclusively in capital letters or special characters. Read more on the Ministry of the Interior and Housing's website here about the rules for which party names can be approved.







4. Publication on the voter declaration portal
If your party name is approved, the Ministry of the Interior and
Housing will immediately set up a
collection for the party on the voter declaration portal, where
voters will be able to find the party and submit a
[████]

The party is established and published with the information
specified in the application form, i.e. with the party's
name, contact information, the name of the holder of
the party (or a possible representative of the party), and possibly with
a link to the party's own internet page.

The information about the party will be deleted from the voter declaration portal again when the party name approval or any party registration expires, or if the party notifies the ministry that the party is dissolved.




5. Processing of personal data

The Ministry of the Interior and Housing is responsible for the handling of the personal data that we receive in connection with your application for approval of a new party name. Read on the Ministry of the Interior and Housing's website here about how the ministry processes your personal data.






Ministry of the Interior and Housing, June 2021
